# UIAO AWS SaaS {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
This page is the operator-facing articulation of the **UIAO AWS SaaS**
deployment — the same multi-tenant governance plane as
[UIAO Azure SaaS](./azure-saas.qmd), running on a second cloud. The normative
source is [ADR-117](../../adr/adr-117-aws-saas-surface.qmd); the implementation
lives in the `uiao.saas` package and `deploy/aws/`. The in-repo companion to
this page is
[`deploy/aws/README.md`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/deploy/aws/README.md).
:::

::: {.callout-important}
**Status — shipped but dormant, synth-validated not deploy-validated.** The
application code is merged and tested; the CDK app **synthesizes** cleanly in CI
(`.github/workflows/cdk-synth.yml`) but has **not** yet been deployed against a
real AWS account. Treat this page as the target operating model; deploy-time
validation against a live account is a tracked follow-up (ADR-117 "Deferred").
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## One application, two clouds
The `uiao.saas` application is unchanged between Azure and AWS — same control
plane, tenancy, per-plan quotas, audit trail, and `application/problem+json`
errors ([ADR-115](../../adr/adr-115-saas-production-readiness.qmd)). Only the
*deployment substrate* differs, and that difference is small: the IaC, the
passwordless-DB token source, and the per-tenant resource stamps. This page is
the AWS half of that story; [UIAO Azure SaaS](./azure-saas.qmd) is the Azure
half.
:::

## 1. What this is

UIAO's multi-tenant SaaS plane runs `uiao.saas.asgi:app` — the existing
`uiao.api` data plane plus the SaaS control plane and tenant-resolution
middleware — on **AWS ECS Fargate** behind an Application Load Balancer,
against an **RDS PostgreSQL** tenant registry. One operated service governs
**many** customer Entra tenants, exactly as on Azure: each customer grants
admin consent to the UIAO multi-tenant app registration, and UIAO acquires
per-tenant Microsoft Graph / ARM tokens to run governance passes.

The AWS surface is **parallel to, not a replacement for**, the Azure surface
(ADR-096) and the single-tenant Windows/IIS surface. It exists so programs
standardised on AWS can run UIAO's SaaS plane natively.

## 2. Why ECS Fargate + RDS

| Concern | Azure (ADR-096) | AWS (ADR-117) |
|---|---|---|
| Compute | Container Apps | **ECS Fargate** behind an ALB |
| Tenant registry | PostgreSQL Flexible Server | **RDS PostgreSQL** |
| Passwordless DB | Entra token-as-password | **RDS IAM** token-as-password |
| Per-tenant secrets | Key Vault | **Secrets Manager** |
| Evidence bundles | Blob Storage | **S3** |
| Governance principal | Managed identity | **IAM task role** |
| Logs | Log Analytics | **CloudWatch** |

Fargate is the AWS analogue of Container Apps: serverless containers, managed
ingress/TLS via the ALB, no node fleet to operate. The **task role** is the
governance principal — the AWS equivalent of the managed identity — and the
same cloud-resolution conventions select boundary-correct Graph/ARM audiences.

## 3. Architecture

![UIAO AWS SaaS architecture: customer Entra tenants send inbound JWTs to an Application Load Balancer fronting an ECS Fargate service running uiao.saas.asgi:app (data plane + control plane), which uses its IAM task role for per-tenant Graph/ARM tokens and an RDS IAM token for the database, backed by RDS PostgreSQL, Secrets Manager, and an S3 evidence bucket inside a VPC.](images/aws-saas-architecture.svg){#fig-aws-saas-architecture fig-alt="Engineering blueprint diagram on a white background. Three boxes at top labeled Customer tenant A, B, C send an inbound JWT arrow down to an Application Load Balancer box. Below it a large box labeled VPC contains an ECS Fargate service box running uiao.saas.asgi:app with a Data plane and Control plane, holding a pill labeled IAM task role. Three arrows descend to three boxes labeled RDS PostgreSQL tenant registry, Secrets Manager per-tenant secrets, and S3 evidence bundles. A note reads passwordless: RDS IAM token as DB password. 16:9 landscape, no human figures." width="100%"}

The two planes share one process, a `/healthz` liveness endpoint, and a
`/readyz` readiness endpoint (the ALB target-group health check):

- **Data plane.** Every non-public request carries an Entra access token.
  `TenantResolutionMiddleware` verifies it, resolves the `tid` claim to a
  registered tenant, rejects non-onboarded / non-active tenants with `403`
  problem+json, enforces the tenant's plan rate limit, and binds a
  `TenantContext` for the request.
- **Control plane.** `POST /control/v1/tenants` and the lifecycle routes
  require a publisher-tenant token carrying the `UIAO.SaaS.Admin` app role.

## 4. Tenancy and data isolation

Tenancy is identical to the Azure surface: each customer is a `Tenant`
identified by its Entra GUID, carrying a lifecycle status, a plan, and a
deterministic **`data_namespace`**. On AWS that namespace scopes the RDS
schema, the **S3 key prefix**, and the **Secrets Manager name prefix**
(`uiao/<namespace>/…`). The lifecycle state machine
(`PENDING → ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED → DEPROVISIONED`) and the rule that only
`ACTIVE` tenants receive governance traffic are unchanged.

## 5. Prerequisites

1. An AWS account and a target **region**.
2. The **CDK toolchain**: `npm install -g aws-cdk@2`, plus the app's
   deploy-time deps (`pip install -r deploy/aws/requirements.txt`).
3. A **CDK bootstrap** in the account/region (`cdk bootstrap`) — once.
4. The same **multi-tenant Entra app registration** as the Azure surface
   (UIAO governs Entra tenants regardless of where the SaaS runs): an
   Application ID URI (e.g. `api://uiao`), the Graph/ARM application
   permissions, and the `UIAO.SaaS.Admin` app role. See
   [Azure SaaS §14](./azure-saas.qmd#entra-app-registration-walkthrough).
5. A built **`uiao-saas` container image** pushed to **ECR** (the cloud-neutral
   image — same `deploy/azure/Dockerfile`).

## 6. Configuration

The container reads the same `UIAO_SAAS_*` variables as the Azure surface
(`uiao.saas.settings.SaasSettings`); the CDK stack wires them:

| Variable | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `UIAO_SAAS_DATABASE_URL` | SQLAlchemy async DSN — **passwordless** (no password) | CDK (RDS endpoint) |
| `UIAO_SAAS_DATABASE_USE_AWS_IAM_AUTH` | `true` — authenticate to RDS with an IAM token (ADR-117) | CDK |
| `UIAO_SAAS_AWS_REGION` | Region for IAM token signing + stamp clients | CDK |
| `UIAO_SAAS_AWS_S3_BUCKET` | Evidence-bundle bucket (per-tenant prefixes) | CDK (S3) |
| `UIAO_SAAS_AWS_SECRETS_PREFIX` | Secrets Manager prefix for per-tenant scopes | Operator (default `uiao`) |
| `UIAO_SAAS_APP_CLIENT_ID` | UIAO multi-tenant app client ID | App registration |
| `UIAO_SAAS_PUBLISHER_TENANT_ID` | Home tenant that owns the control plane | Operator |
| `UIAO_SAAS_API_AUDIENCE` | Audience inbound tokens must carry | App registration |
| `UIAO_SAAS_CLOUD` | `commercial` (also GCC-Moderate), `gcc-high`, `dod` | Operator |
| `UIAO_SAAS_RATE_LIMITING_ENABLED` | Per-tenant rate limiting (default on) | Operator |
| `UIAO_SAAS_AUDIT_ENABLED` | Audit trail + `GET /control/v1/audit` (default on) | Operator |
| `UIAO_SAAS_STAMP_EXECUTION_ENABLED` | Execute per-tenant resource stamps | Operator (default off) |

## 7. Deploy

```bash
cd deploy/aws
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
npm install -g aws-cdk@2

# Synthesize (no AWS account needed — same as the CI gate)
cdk synth -c environmentName=dev

# Deploy (uses your AWS credentials)
cdk bootstrap                      # once per account/region
cdk deploy -c environmentName=dev \
  -c imageUri=<acct>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/uiao-saas:latest \
  -c appClientId=<client-id> -c publisherTenantId=<tenant-guid>
```

The stack (`deploy/aws/uiao_saas_stack.py`) provisions a VPC, RDS PostgreSQL
(IAM auth, private subnets, encrypted), an ECS Fargate service + ALB running
`uiao.saas.asgi:app`, an S3 evidence bucket (TLS-enforced, private, versioned),
and the IAM task role. Every change under `deploy/aws/` is compile-validated by
`cdk synth` in CI (`.github/workflows/cdk-synth.yml`), credential-free, before
any deploy.

### 7.1 One-time DB role bootstrap

RDS IAM auth requires the `uiao_app` role to exist with the `rds_iam` role
granted. After the first deploy, connect once as the master user (from the
generated Secrets Manager secret) and run:

```sql
CREATE USER uiao_app;
GRANT rds_iam TO uiao_app;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE uiao TO uiao_app;
```

This is the AWS counterpart of binding the managed identity as the Postgres
Entra administrator on Azure — it is a data-plane (SQL) step, not expressible
in CDK.

## 8. Onboarding a tenant

Identical to the Azure surface — the control-plane API is the same:

```bash
curl -X POST https://<alb-dns>/control/v1/tenants \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant_id": "<customer-tenant-guid>", "display_name": "Acme", "plan": "standard"}'
```

The response includes the admin-consent URL and the planned per-tenant stamp
steps. With `UIAO_SAAS_STAMP_EXECUTION_ENABLED` set, the `AwsStampExecutor`
provisions the tenant's RDS schema, S3 prefix, and Secrets Manager scope, each
named after its `data_namespace`.

## 9. Lifecycle operations

The lifecycle routes are cloud-independent — see
[Azure SaaS §9](./azure-saas.qmd#lifecycle-operations). `GET /control/v1/audit`
returns the control-plane audit trail (admin only).

## 10. Security model

- **Inbound.** Tokens are signature-verified against the issuing tenant's JWKS
  (RS256) in production; the dev-only unsigned switch defaults off.
- **Authorization.** The data plane rejects non-onboarded / non-active tenants;
  the control plane requires the `UIAO.SaaS.Admin` app role.
- **No long-lived database password.** RDS IAM authentication is enabled and
  the task role holds `rds-db:connect` on the `uiao_app` user; the app mints a
  short-lived IAM token as the connection password (`uiao.saas.aws_pg_auth`).
- **Private, encrypted data tier.** RDS is not publicly accessible and is
  reachable only from the service security group; the evidence bucket enforces
  TLS, blocks public access, and is encrypted + versioned.
- **Error surface.** RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` on both planes.

## 11. Production-readiness

The AWS surface carries the same production-readiness layer as Azure
([ADR-115](../../adr/adr-115-saas-production-readiness.qmd)): per-plan quotas +
per-tenant rate limiting (`429` + `RateLimit-*` headers), the
`GET /control/v1/audit` trail, problem+json errors, and the **`/readyz`**
readiness probe — which here backs the **ALB target-group health check**, so a
task that cannot reach RDS is withheld from the load-balancer pool. The
passwordless RDS IAM auth (ADR-117) is the AWS realization of the ADR-116
passwordless doctrine, sharing the same SQLAlchemy `do_connect` token seam as
the Entra provider.

## 12. Local development

Local dev is cloud-neutral — the in-memory registry needs no AWS:

```bash
pip install -e ".[aws]"
export UIAO_SAAS_INSECURE_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_TOKENS=true   # dev ONLY
export UIAO_SAAS_API_AUDIENCE=api://uiao
export UIAO_SAAS_PUBLISHER_TENANT_ID=<your-tenant-guid>
uvicorn uiao.saas.asgi:app --reload
```

`tests/test_saas_aws_pg_auth.py` and `tests/test_saas_aws_stamp.py` cover the
RDS IAM token cache and the AWS stamp executor against fakes (no boto3, no AWS).

## 13. Sovereign clouds (GovCloud)

`UIAO_SAAS_CLOUD` selects the Entra boundary for the tenants UIAO governs, the
same as on Azure. The AWS *substrate* itself in **GovCloud (US)** is not a
target of ADR-117: the RDS IAM endpoint and partition ARNs (`aws-us-gov`) would
need verification for a GovCloud stamp — a listed review trigger. No GovCloud
SaaS is stood up today.

## 14. Post-deployment validation

```bash
# ALB DNS
ALB=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name uiao-saas-dev \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='LoadBalancerDns'].OutputValue" -o text)

# Liveness + readiness
curl -sf "https://$ALB/healthz" && echo "PASS: /healthz"
curl -sf "https://$ALB/readyz"  && echo "PASS: /readyz (registry reachable)"

# Data plane — expect 403 problem+json (no tenant) not 401/500
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://$ALB/api/v1/orgtree/status"
```

## 15. Monitoring (CloudWatch)

ECS Fargate ships container logs and metrics to CloudWatch (Container Insights
is enabled on the cluster). Useful signals:

```bash
# Tail the service logs
aws logs tail /ecs/uiao-saas-dev --follow

# 5xx at the load balancer (CloudWatch metric)
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics \
  --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --metric-name HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count \
  --start-time "$(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%FT%TZ)" --end-time "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
  --period 300 --statistics Sum
```

The tenant lifecycle audit is cloud-independent: `GET /control/v1/audit`.

## 16. Disaster recovery

| Component | Recovery path | Typical RTO |
|---|---|---|
| Fargate service | `cdk deploy` (idempotent) | ~10 min |
| RDS PostgreSQL | Point-in-time restore to a new instance (7-day backup) | ~20–40 min |
| Secrets Manager | 7-day recovery window on delete | ~5 min |
| S3 evidence | Versioned + retained; cross-region replication optional | ~min |
| End-to-end | All above in sequence | ~1 h |

After an RDS restore, re-run the §7.1 role bootstrap on the restored instance
and update `UIAO_SAAS_DATABASE_URL` to its endpoint (the DSN stays
passwordless; the app re-authenticates with an IAM token).
